objective.name: sandbox.py.call.cpp
objective.description: Python wrapper-backed capacity that awaits a user capacity served by the C++ wrapper

#root.role: Emit a wrapper-to-wrapper user-capacity call from Python to C++ and return the awaited remote result.

effects.wrapper_runtime: The interpreted Python wrapper runtime may be started lazily.
effects.cross_wrapper_route: The Python wrapper emits an awaited user-capacity call toward the C++ wrapper.

transformation_contract.morphing: A Python wrapper request becomes a remote C++ wrapper response returned through one awaited cross-wrapper engine route.
invariants: sandbox.py.call.cpp must remain bounded by its declared inputs, outputs, and effects.
Internal implementation strategy may vary, but the declared contract surface must remain stable.
success: sandbox.py.call.cpp returns payload and matter effects consistent with the declared outputs when it succeeds.
Successful execution preserves the semantic change described by morphing.
failure: sandbox.py.call.cpp fails when required inputs or matter contracts are not satisfied.
The capacity fails when the underlying runtime or wrapper cannot satisfy the declared contract.
notes: This contract constrains expected behavior and observable effects, not the internal implementation decomposition.
Humans and LLMs should interpret the capacity through the declared interface and semantic guarantees first.

subjective.intent: prove wrapper to wrapper call through the engine
